name: Moksy support
description: Answering Moksy customers from its own published pages: contact routes, plans and limits, MOX and refunds, reviews, error messages, trust and the terms.

groups.contact: Moksy contact route or report detail

cards.subject: The support address
says: is support@moksy.ai
is the route for account, sign-in, plan, billing, review and breakage problems
cards.use: need to report a broken feature or a sign-in problem to a person
not: handles privacy and data requests

cards.subject: The privacy address
says: is privacy@moksy.ai
reaches the people who handle privacy and data requests directly
cards.use: hear a customer ask for access to or deletion of their data
not: handles billing questions about a charge

cards.subject: The legal address
says: is legal@moksy.ai
takes questions about the wording of the terms
cards.use: are asked about what a clause in the Terms of Service means
not: takes sign-in problems from locked-out customers

cards.subject: Sales
says: handles pricing and procurement enquiries for someone buying rather than fixing
is where the contact page sends quotes for large teams
cards.use: meet a customer who wants a quote rather than a fix
not: arbitrates disputed reviews

cards.subject: The help centre
says: is where the contact page says most answers already are
comes before writing to a person
cards.use: want to check whether a question is already answered before writing in
not: replaces the privacy address for data requests

cards.subject: Account email and plan or review link
says: are the two things the contact page asks every message to include
roughly halve the number of messages it takes to fix something
cards.use: want to cut the back-and-forth on a customer's problem
not: are replaced by the customer's card number

cards.subject: Billing details to include
says: are the date and amount of the charge
let support find the transaction without asking again
cards.use: hear a customer say a charge looks wrong
not: are the customer's full card number
like: Account email and plan or review link

cards.subject: Locked-out report
says: is made by saying so from the address on the account
tells support the customer cannot sign in at all
cards.use: are writing to a customer who cannot sign in at all
not: can be sent from any address the customer likes

cards.subject: Plan-looks-wrong report
says: names the section that looks wrong
says whether a reviewer has been involved
cards.use: hear a customer say their plan has an error in it
not: needs only the customer's name
like: Account email and plan or review link

cards.subject: Broken-feature report
says: says what the customer did and what happened
is helped by a screenshot, worth several paragraphs
cards.use: are asked how a customer should describe something that is broken
not: needs only the name of the browser

cards.subject: Review dispute route
says: goes in through support
ends with arbitration by a senior reviewer
cards.use: hear a customer disagree with the verdict of a review
not: goes to Sales, which handles pricing

cards.subject: The Free plan
says: costs £0 a month
gives 3 projects, 5 exports a month and 1 seat
has no Expert Reviews and no API access
cards.use: are asked what a customer gets before paying anything
not: includes unlimited Expert Reviews

cards.subject: The Pro plan
says: costs £19 a month
gives 25 projects, 5 seats and 100 exports a month
is the first tier an accredited reviewer can read a plan on
cards.use: meet a customer who needs Expert Reviews and a small team
not: gives unlimited seats

cards.subject: The Max plan
says: costs £79 a month
gives unlimited projects, seats and exports
is the plan that makes someone eligible to become a paid reviewer
cards.use: are asked which plan allows a person to become a paid reviewer
not: gives only 25 projects

cards.subject: The Starter Blueprint
says: covers 5 of the 22 areas
is the Blueprint depth that comes with the Free plan
cards.use: are asked how many areas a Free customer's Blueprint covers
not: covers all 22 areas

cards.subject: The Fuller Blueprint
says: covers 12 of the 22 areas
is the Blueprint depth that comes with the Pro plan
cards.use: are asked how many areas a Pro customer's Blueprint covers
not: covers only 5 areas

cards.subject: The Complete Blueprint
says: covers all 22 areas
is the Blueprint depth that comes with the Max plan
cards.use: are asked what a Max customer's Blueprint covers
not: covers 12 of the 22 areas

cards.subject: Enterprise and public sector pricing
says: is priced separately from the published plans
includes SSO and SCIM, role-based access and a signed DPA
includes invoicing against a PO, UK data residency and a private reviewer pool
cards.use: meet a university asking for SSO, SCIM and invoicing against a PO
not: is listed as a monthly price on the pricing page

cards.subject: Public body procurement support
says: gives public bodies procurement paperwork and discounted credit
sits within the separately priced Enterprise and public sector offer
cards.use: hear a public body ask what procurement help is available
not: is included in the Free plan

cards.subject: The Free plan's status
says: is described by the pricing page as a real plan, not a teaser
is the same engine reporting on fewer areas
is deliberately enough to judge whether the thinking is any good
cards.use: are asked whether the Free plan is a trial or a real plan
not: is described as a short trial that expires

cards.subject: API access
says: is included on Pro and Max
is not included on Free
cards.use: are asked which published plans include API access
not: is included on Free

cards.subject: Access to published reviewer work
says: is included on the Free plan for reading
is different from a reviewer reading and correcting the customer's own plan
cards.use: hear a Free customer think they can have a reviewer correct their own plan
not: lets a Free customer commission unlimited reviews

cards.subject: Moksy's claim over customer ideas
says: is none: Moksy claims no rights over a customer's plan or the idea behind it
applies on every tier
cards.use: hear a founder worry that Moksy owns their idea
not: is a licence over the idea on Free only

cards.subject: MOX
says: is Moksy credit
is worth $0.01 per MOX in the lexicon
cards.use: are asked what MOX is
not: is a monthly membership that renews on its own

cards.subject: Membership
says: is a monthly plan that carries what is included in it
renews on its own
cards.use: need to explain how a plan differs from credit
not: is credit bought once and spent when chosen

cards.subject: What MOX pays for
says: covers work outside plan benefits such as expert reviews, additional plans and priority turnaround
is spent when the customer chooses
cards.use: are asked what a customer can spend MOX on
not: is needed before any plan can be produced

cards.subject: Producing a plan without MOX
says: needs no MOX purchase at all
is possible on any tier
cards.use: hear a customer say they must buy MOX before they can produce a plan
not: requires a minimum MOX balance of one review

cards.subject: MOX renewal
says: does not happen on its own
means credit is bought once
cards.use: are asked whether MOX renews each month like a plan
not: is automatic each month

cards.subject: Dollar peg
says: keeps MOX tied to dollars
stops the price of a review moving with the customer's currency
cards.use: are asked why a review costs the same MOX in any currency
not: makes MOX fall in value each month

cards.subject: Wallet ledger
says: itemises every debit
lets a customer see what a piece of work cost after it happened
cards.use: are asked to explain why a customer's balance dropped
not: shows only the current balance with no history

cards.subject: Pooled MOX balance
says: is one balance for the whole workspace on team tiers
replaces a card per person
cards.use: hear a team ask how credit is shared between members
not: gives each member a separate balance

cards.subject: MOX expiry
says: has no expiry surprises as balance and history stay visible in the wallet
is something the customer can check themselves
cards.use: hear a customer worry their credit will vanish
not: is stated as a fixed number of days

cards.subject: Unused credit refund request
says: is answered by the page with contact support and we will look at it
is a discretionary review, not a promise of an automatic refund
cards.use: hear a customer ask for a refund of unused credit
not: is promised as an automatic full refund

cards.subject: Review refund rule
says: is not published anywhere in the sources
means support must never quote a refund amount for a review
cards.use: are asked what Moksy will refund for a review that disappointed
not: is a full refund within 14 days

cards.subject: The Identity Verification Failed message
says: says the email or password entered was invalid
means the sign-in details were wrong
cards.use: hear a customer quote 'Invalid email or password'
not: means the account is locked

cards.subject: The secure session expired message
says: says re-authentication is required
means the customer should sign in again
cards.use: hear a customer say their secure session has expired
not: means the account has been closed

cards.subject: The Identity Suspended message
says: says there were too many failed attempts
means the account is locked
is reported to support from the address on the account
cards.use: hear a customer quote 'Too many failed attempts. Contact administration'
not: means a wrong password was typed once

cards.subject: The Multi-Factor Authentication message
says: says the process needs an extra verification step to proceed
relates to the two-factor requirement for administrators
cards.use: hear a customer say they are asked for extra verification
not: says the account is locked

cards.subject: The email already registered message
says: says that email already has a Moksy account
suggests logging in instead
cards.use: hear a customer say sign-up refuses their email address
not: says the password was wrong

cards.subject: The Access Restricted message
says: says the feature is not included in the current subscription
is a plan limit, not a fault
cards.use: hear a customer quote 'not included in your current subscription'
not: means the customer's role lacks permission

cards.subject: The Authority Denied message
says: says the customer lacks the required role for the module
is a role or permission issue, not a plan issue
cards.use: hear a customer quote 'do not have the required role for this module'
not: means the plan does not include the feature

cards.subject: The read-only message
says: says the customer has read-only permissions for the resource
comes from a read-only role
cards.use: hear a customer quote 'read-only permissions for this resource'
not: means the subscription lacks the feature

cards.subject: The timeout message
says: says the request exceeded the 10,000ms safety threshold
reports a timeout
cards.use: hear a customer quote the 10,000ms safety threshold
not: says engineers have been alerted

cards.subject: The scheduled governance message
says: says the platform is undergoing scheduled governance
tells the customer to check back shortly
cards.use: hear a customer say the platform says to check back shortly
not: tells the customer to refresh the interface

cards.subject: The system update message
says: says a critical system update is available
tells the customer to refresh the interface
cards.use: hear a customer quote 'Please refresh your interface'
not: says the platform is in maintenance mode

cards.subject: The orchestration error message
says: says an unexpected orchestration error occurred and engineers have been alerted
is an internal error, so the useful question is what the customer did and what happened
cards.use: hear a customer quote an unexpected orchestration error
not: is a plan limit

cards.subject: UK data residency
says: holds primary data in the UK
pins sub-processors to UK or EEA regions wherever the service supports it
cards.use: are asked where customer data is held
not: holds primary data in the US

cards.subject: Encryption
says: uses TLS 1.2 or better in transit
uses AES-256 at rest for the primary database and its backups
cards.use: are asked how data is protected in transit and at rest
not: is stated as end-to-end with keys held by the customer

cards.subject: Access controls
says: are role-based with a per-endpoint audit log
include quarterly access reviews
cards.use: are asked how access to customer data is controlled
not: are a single shared login for all staff

cards.subject: Administrator two-factor authentication
says: is mandatory for administrators
is listed among the access controls
cards.use: hear a customer ask whether admins must use two-factor
not: is optional for all users

cards.subject: Personal data sale
says: never happens: Moksy does not sell personal data
includes no enrichment with third-party demographic feeds
cards.use: hear a customer ask whether their data is sold
not: is allowed with consent

cards.subject: Breach notification
says: tells controllers within 72 hours of Moksy becoming aware of a personal-data breach
follows UK GDPR Article 33
cards.use: are asked how quickly controllers hear about a breach
not: promises notice within 24 hours

cards.subject: Anonymised audit and ledger rows
says: are anonymised rather than deleted
exist for fraud detection and financial record-keeping
cards.use: hear a customer ask why some records survive a deletion request
not: are deleted the same day as the account

cards.subject: ISO 27001 status
says: is not held: Moksy is not ISO 27001 certified
is stated plainly on the trust page
cards.use: hear a buyer ask 'Are you ISO 27001 certified?'
not: is held and in date

cards.subject: Cyber Essentials status
says: is not yet held, and the page says it will change if that changes
is stated plainly on the trust page
cards.use: hear a buyer ask about Cyber Essentials
not: is held with a published certificate number

cards.subject: The DPA
says: covers Moksy's use of large language models to draft plans
is the signed agreement offered on Enterprise and public sector tiers
cards.use: hear a buyer ask which agreement covers the use of AI models
not: is replaced by the Free plan terms

cards.subject: Sub-processor notice
says: takes 30 days' notice when a sub-processor is added
is covered by the DPA
cards.use: are asked how much warning customers get before a new sub-processor
not: takes 24 hours' notice

cards.subject: Listed sub-processors
says: are OpenAI, Stripe, MongoDB Atlas and Redis
are named in the privacy policy
cards.use: are asked which sub-processors the privacy policy lists
not: include only Stripe

cards.subject: Card payment handling
says: is done by Stripe
means Moksy does not store card numbers
cards.use: hear a customer ask whether Moksy stores their card number
not: keeps card numbers in the main database

cards.subject: The data controller
says: is Moksy AI Ltd, reached at privacy@moksy.ai
is named in the privacy policy
cards.use: are asked who the data controller is
not: is Stripe

cards.subject: Data subject rights
says: include access, correction, deletion, objection or restriction, and portability
include a right to complain to the ICO
cards.use: hear a customer ask what rights they have over their data
not: are limited to a right to cancel

cards.subject: Cookie consent
says: lets strictly necessary cookies run without consent
needs explicit consent for optional analytics cookies
cards.use: are asked which cookies need consent
not: is needed for strictly necessary cookies

cards.subject: The contracting company
says: is Moksy AI Ltd, registered in England and Wales
is the party the customer agrees with
cards.use: are asked who the Terms are an agreement with
not: is Stripe

cards.subject: Governing law
says: is English law, with English courts
applies to the Terms
cards.use: are asked which law governs the Terms
not: is the law of the customer's country

cards.subject: Minimum age
says: is at least 18 to create an account
applies to everyone who accepts the Terms
cards.use: hear a 16-year-old ask to open an account
not: is 13

cards.subject: Authority to bind
says: is represented by someone creating an account for an organisation
means they say they can bind it
cards.use: hear an employee set up an account on behalf of their employer
not: is not needed for organisations

cards.subject: Credential responsibility
says: makes the customer responsible for keeping login credentials confidential
makes the customer responsible for all activity under the account
cards.use: hear a customer blame Moksy for activity done with their shared login
not: makes Moksy responsible for all activity under the account

cards.subject: Acceptable use
says: forbids unlawful use, unauthorised access and reverse engineering
forbids reselling or sublicensing access without written permission
cards.use: hear a customer ask whether they may resell their Moksy access
not: allows resale of access freely

cards.subject: Billing terms
says: bill in advance, monthly or annually
are in GBP and exclude VAT unless stated
authorise recurring charges through Stripe until the customer cancels
cards.use: are asked how paid plans are billed
not: bill in arrears in US dollars

cards.subject: Cancellation
says: can be done any time in account settings
stops the recurring charges
cards.use: hear a customer ask how to cancel
not: needs a letter to legal

cards.subject: Data ownership clause
says: leaves ownership of submitted data and content with the customer
gives Moksy a non-exclusive, royalty-free licence solely to provide the services
cards.use: hear a customer ask who owns what they submit
not: transfers ownership to Moksy

cards.subject: AI output clause
says: says AI output is for information only and is not guaranteed accurate, complete or fit for purpose
makes the customer solely responsible for validating it before relying on it
cards.use: hear a customer say they relied on a figure without checking it
not: guarantees every figure for a year

cards.subject: Liability cap
says: limits Moksy's total liability for a claim to the amount paid in the 12 months before it
excludes liability for indirect or consequential loss
cards.use: hear a customer claim losses far beyond what they paid
not: is unlimited

cards.subject: Change notification
says: tells customers of material changes by email or a prominent notice
treats continued use as acceptance
cards.use: are asked how customers learn about changes to the Terms
not: needs the customer to sign again

cards.subject: Data deletion timeline conflict
says: is that the trust page says hard-deletion within 30 days while the privacy policy says 90 days
is routed to privacy@moksy.ai instead of quoting either figure
cards.use: hear a customer ask exactly how many days data is kept after closing
not: is settled at 30 days

cards.subject: Security questionnaire route conflict
says: is that the contact page says Sales while the trust page says privacy@moksy.ai
means confirming the current route before promising one
cards.use: hear a buyer send a security questionnaire to support
not: is settled as Sales only

cards.subject: Sector wording conflict
says: is that the Terms and privacy policy call Moksy an education-sector service while other pages name founders, teams and the public sector
means telling a founder it is not only for schools and flagging the outdated wording
cards.use: hear a founder ask whether Moksy is only for schools
not: is settled as education only

cards.subject: Review arbitration wording
says: is saying a senior reviewer as published
avoids naming a rung from the internal lexicon
cards.use: are tempted to name the internal rung that arbitrates a dispute
not: is naming the exact internal rung

cards.subject: Review values in MOX
says: are quoted only as published and dated, never as a promise
are not to be confused with what a membership includes
cards.use: are asked what a review is worth in MOX
not: are promised never to change

cards.subject: Quoting published pages
says: means quoting the pages as the company's statements
includes saying you will confirm when pages disagree
cards.use: are tempted to answer from your own memory of how Moksy works
not: means quoting your own understanding

cards.subject: Reporting a discrepancy
says: is passing on the disagreeing pages after helping the customer
lets the pages be corrected
cards.use: notice two published pages disagree
not: is leaving it for the customer to notice

cards.subject: An AI-drafted plan
says: is a draft written by large language models from the customer's answers
is fluent, which makes an unchecked one risky
cards.use: hear a customer treat a generated plan as final
not: is a guaranteed final answer

cards.subject: Expert Review
says: lets an accredited reviewer correct a plan
is included from Pro upward
cards.use: hear a customer ask how a person can check their plan
not: is included on the Free plan

cards.subject: Shown reasoning
says: appears with every recommendation instead of a bare answer
lets a customer judge a claim before relying on it
cards.use: are asked what makes a recommendation checkable
not: is hidden behind the Expert Review

cards.subject: Plan accuracy
says: is acknowledged on the pricing page: a drafted plan can contain errors
is the reason an accredited reviewer can correct it
cards.use: hear a customer ask whether a plan can be wrong
not: is denied on the pricing page

cards.subject: Using the package after generation
says: means reviewing the recommendations internally and refining the output
includes briefing a supplier, comparing options or aligning a delivery team
cards.use: are asked what the help page says to do with a generated package
not: means committing budget immediately

cards.subject: A working brief
says: is how the help page says to use a plan before committing budget
treats the plan as a starting point
cards.use: hear a customer plan to commit budget on a plan alone
not: is a fixed quote

cards.subject: Review debit check
says: starts with the wallet ledger
tells whether MOX was spent on something outside the customer's plan benefits
cards.use: hear a customer ask why a review debited their wallet
not: starts with refunding the customer

cards.subject: Severity
says: rates how badly a problem damages the customer's work
stays the same however loudly the customer writes
cards.use: need to rate how serious a problem is
not: is the order in which the queue is worked

cards.subject: Priority
says: decides the order in which tickets are worked
weighs severity against urgency and commitments
cards.use: need to decide which ticket to handle first
not: rates the damage to the customer alone

cards.subject: Intake questions
says: gather the facts needed before any diagnosis
are the same few questions asked each time for a category
cards.use: receive a vague message that says only 'it does not work'
not: are the final reply

cards.subject: Reproduction steps
says: list the exact actions that cause the problem
let a second person see the same failure
cards.use: need an engineer to see the same fault the customer saw
not: are the customer's feelings about the fault

cards.subject: Duplicate detection
says: links tickets describing the same issue
shows when one fault is affecting many customers
cards.use: notice the third ticket this hour describing the same fault
not: merges two unrelated customers into one account

cards.subject: Categorisation tags
says: label a ticket by type of problem
make later reporting on common issues possible
cards.use: want to report which issues come up most often
not: decide how quickly a ticket must be answered

cards.subject: Workaround
says: gives the customer a way to carry on while the fix is pending
does not remove the underlying fault
cards.use: know a fix will take time but the customer has a deadline
not: is the permanent fix

cards.subject: Root cause
says: is the underlying reason a problem happens
is found by asking why until the explanation stops changing
cards.use: see the same symptom return after each ticket is closed
not: is the first symptom the customer mentioned

cards.subject: First-contact resolution
says: solves the problem in the first reply
depends on gathering the details before answering
cards.use: want the customer to need only one message
not: is closing the ticket without a reply

cards.subject: Active listening
says: means reading the whole message before replying
picks out the customer's actual question beneath the frustration
cards.use: receive a long angry message
not: means replying to the first sentence only

cards.subject: Empathy statement
says: names the customer's feeling and the impact on them
comes before the solution
cards.use: meet a customer who is upset about lost time
not: admits legal fault

cards.subject: Apology that names the problem
says: says sorry for the specific thing that went wrong
avoids vague regret
cards.use: need to apologise for a real failure
not: says sorry you feel that way

cards.subject: Plain language
says: uses short words the customer already uses
explains any unavoidable term
cards.use: are about to reply with internal jargon
not: uses internal codenames for speed

cards.subject: Positive framing
says: says what can be done rather than what cannot
keeps a refusal constructive
cards.use: must refuse a request but offer something else
not: hides the refusal altogether

cards.subject: Setting expectations
says: states what happens next and roughly when
avoids promising what you cannot control
cards.use: cannot fix a problem right now
not: promises a fix by tomorrow regardless

cards.subject: Closing the loop
says: tells the customer the outcome after they reported a problem
shows their report was acted on
cards.use: learn that a bug a customer reported has been fixed
not: waits until the customer asks

cards.subject: The pause before replying
says: is a short delay used to avoid answering anger with anger
helps a reply focus on the problem
cards.use: feel stung by a rude message
not: means replying immediately to match the customer's tone

cards.subject: De-escalation
says: lowers the temperature before solving the problem
includes acknowledging, slowing the pace and focusing on facts
cards.use: face a customer who is shouting in capitals
not: matches the customer's volume

cards.subject: Escalation trigger
says: is a pre-agreed condition that moves a ticket to someone else
includes limits on authority and time
cards.use: are unsure when a ticket must go up
not: is the customer using the word urgent

cards.subject: Warm handoff
says: introduces the customer and context to the next person
spares the customer from repeating the story
cards.use: pass a ticket to a specialist
not: forwards the ticket with no note

cards.subject: Escalation note
says: summarises the facts, steps taken and what is needed
lets the receiver act without re-reading the thread
cards.use: write the hand-over for a specialist
not: is a copy of the whole thread

cards.subject: Ownership during escalation
says: stays with the original agent until a named person accepts
keeps the customer informed
cards.use: have escalated and the customer asks for an update
not: transfers the moment you click escalate

cards.subject: Bug report to engineering
says: gives steps, expected result, actual result and impact
is written so an engineer can act without a call
cards.use: have found a fault that needs engineering
not: says it is broken, please fix

cards.subject: Incident communication
says: gives customers regular, honest updates during an outage
includes what is known, what is not and when the next update comes
cards.use: are told several customers are affected by an outage
not: stays silent until it is resolved

cards.subject: Single source of truth
says: keeps one authoritative version of each answer
stops agents giving different answers
cards.use: find that two agents gave a customer different answers
not: copies the answer into every ticket

cards.subject: Article titled in customer words
says: names an article with the phrase customers search for
makes it findable
cards.use: are writing an article for a common question
not: uses internal project names

cards.subject: Canned reply
says: is a saved response that saves typing
needs personalising before it is sent
cards.use: answer the same question many times a day
not: is sent unchanged to everyone

cards.subject: Review date
says: marks when an article must be checked again
catches stale answers before customers see them
cards.use: worry an article has gone out of date
not: is the date the article was first written

cards.subject: Known-issue article
says: describes a current fault and its workaround
is removed or updated once the fix ships
cards.use: learn of a fault that many customers hit
not: lasts for ever once published

cards.subject: Ticket-driven gap analysis
says: looks at recurring tickets to find missing articles
feeds new articles from real questions
cards.use: see the same question arriving repeatedly
not: is based on what staff think customers need

cards.subject: Identity verification
says: confirms the requester controls the account before changes
is done through details already on file
cards.use: get a request to change an email address
not: is accepting a name given in the message

cards.subject: Data minimisation
says: asks only for the information needed to solve the problem
keeps unnecessary personal data out of tickets
cards.use: are tempted to ask for more details just in case
not: collects everything possible up front

cards.subject: Never ask for passwords
says: is a rule that support never requests a password
keeps secrets out of tickets
cards.use: are about to ask a customer to send their password to diagnose a login
not: is relaxed for urgent cases

cards.subject: Redaction
says: hides sensitive details in screenshots and logs before sharing
protects data when a ticket goes to others
cards.use: receive a screenshot that shows a card number
not: is leaving details visible for speed

cards.subject: Least-privilege access
says: gives each agent only the access the job needs
limits harm from a mistake or misuse
cards.use: are asked who should see full customer records
not: gives all agents full access

cards.subject: Data subject request
says: is a customer's request about their own personal data
should be recognised even if not labelled as one
cards.use: get a message asking what data is held about the customer
not: is handled like a normal query

cards.subject: Breach recognition
says: spots that data may have gone to the wrong person
is reported internally at once
cards.use: realise you sent a reply to the wrong customer
not: waits until the end of the week

cards.subject: Social engineering
says: is manipulating an agent into giving access or data
often uses urgency or authority
cards.use: receive an urgent request from someone claiming to be a director
not: is a technical attack on a server

cards.subject: Entitlement
says: is something the customer is owed under stated terms
is applied the same way for everyone
cards.use: check what the written policy gives the customer
not: is a favour at the agent's discretion

cards.subject: Discretionary decision
says: is a case-by-case judgement not promised in advance
needs a consistent basis
cards.use: are asked for something the policy does not promise
not: is automatic for any request

cards.subject: Goodwill gesture
says: is a voluntary act to repair trust
does not admit that a policy was broken
cards.use: want to repair a bad experience beyond the policy
not: is a legal obligation

cards.subject: Consistency of treatment
says: gives similar cases similar outcomes
protects against accusations of unfairness
cards.use: notice two similar complaints got different outcomes
not: means always granting the biggest remedy

cards.subject: Complaint
says: is an expression of dissatisfaction that needs a response
is recorded and followed through
cards.use: hear a customer say they are dissatisfied and want it recorded
not: is the same as general feedback

cards.subject: Written record of a decision
says: notes what was decided and why
lets any colleague follow up consistently
cards.use: finish a difficult refund conversation
not: lives only in your memory

cards.subject: Saying no well
says: explains the reason, offers an alternative and stays courteous
avoids reading out policy as a wall
cards.use: must decline a request that is outside policy
not: blames the customer

cards.subject: Not promising an unconfirmed outcome
says: refuses to promise what you cannot confirm
says you will check and come back
cards.use: are asked for a refund amount you cannot verify
not: guesses a reasonable sum

cards.subject: First response time
says: measures how long a customer waits for a first human reply
is not the same as the time to resolution
cards.use: are asked how quickly customers hear back
not: measures the time until the ticket is closed

cards.subject: Resolution time
says: measures from the report to the problem being solved
depends on the complexity of the issue
cards.use: are asked how long a problem takes to fix
not: measures only the wait for a first reply

cards.subject: Service level agreement
says: is a written commitment on service standards
carries agreed consequences if missed
cards.use: hear a customer ask what is formally promised
not: is an internal hope with no obligation

cards.subject: Clock pause
says: stops the timer while waiting on the customer
restarts when the customer replies
cards.use: are waiting for the customer to send information
not: stops the clock for ever

cards.subject: Backlog ageing
says: tracks how long open tickets have waited
shows tickets about to be forgotten
cards.use: worry old tickets are being neglected
not: counts only new tickets

cards.subject: Customer satisfaction score
says: asks the customer to rate an interaction
is read alongside the comments left
cards.use: want the customer's own view of a conversation
not: measures resolution speed

qa.q: A customer cannot sign in at all and wants to report it. What does the contact page say?
qa.right: Say so from the address on the account
wrong: Write from any address and attach a photo of their ID
qa.why: Account and sign-in problems go to support, from the address on the account.

qa.q: Which address do you give a customer who wants their data deleted?
qa.right: privacy@moksy.ai
qa.why: Privacy and data requests go to privacy@moksy.ai.

qa.q: A customer asks what MOX is. What is the accurate short answer?
qa.right: Moksy credit, bought once and spent when the customer chooses
wrong: A monthly membership that renews on its own
A required deposit before a first plan
qa.why: MOX is credit; a membership is the monthly plan.

qa.q: A new customer asks if Free is a trial that will expire. What do you say?
qa.right: The pricing page calls it a real plan, the same engine on fewer areas
wrong: Yes, it expires after a month
It is a demo with no Blueprint
qa.why: Free is described as a real plan.

qa.q: A customer says they are not sure whether their question is covered already. Where does the contact page say most answers are?
qa.right: In the help centre
qa.why: Contact a person when the help centre does not answer.

qa.q: A customer's first message just says 'it does not work'. What is the best first reply?
qa.right: Ask what they did, what happened and which plan or section, and for the account email
wrong: Apologise and say a fix is coming
qa.why: Intake questions gather the facts before diagnosis.

qa.q: Which statement about an AI-drafted plan fits the trust page?
qa.right: It is a draft, and its fluency makes an unchecked one risky
wrong: It is a verified final answer
It is correct if it reads well
It cannot contain errors on Max
qa.why: The trust page says a draft is fluent, which is the risk.

qa.q: A Free customer says 'Your plan covers only a few areas.' How many areas does the Free Blueprint cover?
qa.right: 5 of the 22
qa.why: Free is a Starter Blueprint of 5 of 22 areas.

qa.q: A customer on Pro asks how many people can share the workspace seats. What is the published figure?
qa.right: 5 seats
qa.why: Pro gives 5 seats; 25 is its project count.

qa.q: A customer sees 'Access Restricted: This feature is not included in your current subscription.' What do you tell them?
qa.right: It is a plan limit, not a fault; the feature is not on their plan
qa.why: Plan limit versus role versus lock are different messages.

qa.q: A customer sees 'Authority Denied: You do not have the required role for this module.' What is it?
qa.right: A role or permission issue, not a plan issue
qa.why: The workspace administrator controls roles.

qa.q: A customer quotes 'Multi-Factor Authentication required to proceed.' What does it mean?
qa.right: An extra verification step is needed before they can continue
qa.why: It is an extra verification step.

qa.q: Which statement about the Terms is accurate?
qa.right: A subscription can be cancelled any time in account settings
qa.why: Cancellation is in account settings.

qa.q: A customer asks if buying MOX is needed to produce a plan. What is accurate?
qa.right: No, nobody needs to buy MOX to produce a plan
wrong: Yes, at least one review is needed
qa.why: MOX is for work outside plan benefits.

qa.q: A customer sends a vague bug report. Which two details most speed a fix?
qa.right: What they did and what happened, plus a screenshot
wrong: Their job title and company size
qa.why: The contact page asks for what they did and what happened.

qa.q: A customer is angry and writes in capitals. What is the best first move?
qa.right: Acknowledge the frustration, then move to the facts
qa.why: De-escalate before solving.

qa.q: A Pro customer says they only get 10 exports a month. What should you check?
qa.right: The published figure of 100 exports a month on Pro, then their usage
wrong: Whether they are on Free, which has 100
Tell them exports are unlimited on Pro
qa.why: Free has 5 exports, Pro 100, Max unlimited; always check the plan.

qa.q: A customer asks you to confirm Moksy is ISO 27001 certified so they can sign. What is the honest answer?
qa.right: No, the trust page says it is not ISO 27001 certified, and you say so plainly
wrong: Yes, it is in progress and will be done soon
Say you do not know and avoid the question
qa.why: Never answer security claims you cannot evidence.

qa.q: A buyer asks where their data is held. What do you say?
qa.right: Primary data is held in the UK, with sub-processors pinned to UK or EEA regions where the service supports it
qa.why: The trust page states UK primary data.

qa.q: A customer asks if Moksy sells personal data. What do you say?
qa.right: No, Moksy does not sell personal data or enrich it with third-party demographic feeds
wrong: It is covered by legitimate interests
qa.why: Stated plainly on the trust page.

qa.q: A customer on Free asks for an Expert Review of their plan. What is accurate?
qa.right: Free has no Expert Reviews; they are included from Pro upward, or can be bought with MOX
wrong: Reviews are not available to customers
qa.why: Expert Review is part of Pro and Max benefits and also MOX work.

qa.q: A customer wants to know whether Moksy owns the plan it produced. What is the answer?
qa.right: Moksy claims no rights over the plan or the idea behind it, and the customer owns the data they submit
wrong: Moksy owns the plan on Free
qa.why: Pricing page and Terms both say so.

qa.q: A customer disputes a review verdict. What is the published route?
qa.right: Write to support; a senior reviewer arbitrates
qa.why: Support is the route in.

qa.q: Which of these is the best escalation note?
qa.right: A summary of the problem, steps already tried, the customer's impact and what you need from the next person
wrong: The whole thread forwarded without comment
A note saying the customer is angry
qa.why: A good note lets the receiver act without re-reading.

qa.q: A customer has been passed to a second agent and asks again for the same details. What went wrong?
qa.right: The handoff was cold and context was not passed on
wrong: The second agent was too senior
The ticket was escalated too soon
qa.why: Warm handoffs carry context.

qa.q: A customer asks you to look at their account after sending only a name. What should you do before changing anything?
qa.right: Confirm they control the account using details already on file
wrong: Make the change; the name is enough
Ask them to send their card number
qa.why: Identity verification before account changes.

qa.q: A customer pastes a screenshot showing a full card number into a ticket. What should you do?
qa.right: Redact it, remind them not to share card details, and carry on with what you need
wrong: Leave it so the team can see everything
Save it in the knowledge base
qa.why: Minimise sensitive data in tickets.

qa.q: What is the difference between severity and priority?
qa.right: Severity rates the damage to the customer; priority decides the order of work
wrong: Priority rates the damage; severity the order
Severity is set by the customer's tone
qa.why: Both are needed in triage.

qa.q: A customer asks how to see what a review cost. Where do they look?
qa.right: The wallet ledger, which itemises every debit
wrong: A monthly statement from Stripe only
qa.why: Every debit is itemised.

qa.q: A customer asks exactly how long Moksy keeps their data after they close their account. What is the best answer?
qa.right: Say the published pages differ, you will confirm, and route to privacy@moksy.ai
wrong: 30 days, as the trust page says
90 days, as the privacy policy says
qa.why: The sources disagree, so neither is definitive.

qa.q: A buyer sends you a security questionnaire and asks if support will answer it. What do you do?
qa.right: Confirm the current route before promising anything; the pages name different routes
qa.why: Contact page says Sales, trust page says privacy@moksy.ai.

qa.q: A founder asks whether Moksy is only for schools because the Terms mention education. What is accurate?
qa.right: No; other pages describe founders, teams, agencies, enterprises and the public sector, and the legal wording is outdated and should be flagged
qa.why: Do not repeat outdated sector wording as settled.

qa.q: A customer asks what Moksy will refund them for a review that disappointed. What is the sound response?
qa.right: No refund rule for reviews is published, so you will not quote an amount; ask support to look into it
qa.why: Never invent a refund rule.

qa.q: A customer asks for a refund of unused MOX credit. What does the page say?
qa.right: Contact support and we will look at it, a discretionary review
qa.why: A discretionary review is not a promise.

qa.q: A customer says the cost figure in a plan was wrong and they paid more to a supplier. What is the accurate position?
qa.right: The plan is a draft, AI output is informational only and the customer must validate it; Expert Review is how a person checks
wrong: Figures are always accurate on Max
qa.why: Terms and pricing page say so.

qa.q: A customer asks what an Expert Review is worth in MOX. What is the sound response?
qa.right: Quote any figure only as published and dated, say the rate can change, and remind them Pro and Max include Expert Reviews
wrong: Promise the figure will never change
Quote the lowest you have seen
qa.why: Review values are quoted as published and dated.

qa.q: A customer says 'The request exceeded the 10,000ms safety threshold'. What is it?
qa.right: A timeout
qa.why: It reports a timeout.

qa.q: A customer reports 'An unexpected orchestration error occurred. Our engineers have been alerted.' What do you ask?
qa.right: What they did and what happened, with a screenshot if possible
wrong: Nothing; the engineers will fix it
qa.why: Internal error; gather steps for reproduction.

qa.q: A university asks for SSO, SCIM, a signed DPA, invoicing against a PO and UK data residency. What does the pricing page say?
qa.right: Enterprise and public sector are priced separately and include those; Sales handles the enquiry
qa.why: Enterprise includes those and is priced separately.

qa.q: A ticket reaches you after two escalations, and the customer is waiting. Who owns it?
qa.right: Whoever has accepted it by name, and they update the customer
wrong: The original agent without telling anyone
qa.why: One named owner at each step.

qa.q: A customer asks you for a discount outside any published policy. What is the best reply?
qa.right: Explain what you can offer within policy and offer to pass the request to someone who can decide, without promising an outcome
qa.why: Do not promise what you cannot confirm.

qa.q: You realise a reply with another customer's details went to the wrong person. What first?
qa.right: Report it internally at once so it can be handled as a possible data breach
wrong: Wait to see if anyone notices
Ask the recipient to ignore it and say nothing
qa.why: Prompt reporting matters.

qa.q: A public-sector officer emails support: 'Are you ISO 27001 certified? Where is our data held? How long until we are told of a breach?' What is the best answer?
qa.right: Answer from the trust page: not ISO 27001 certified, primary data in the UK, controllers told within 72 hours, and offer the Sales route for the questionnaire after confirming it
wrong: Say yes to ISO 27001 to avoid losing the deal
qa.why: State what is published and what is not.

qa.q: You find the help page and the pricing page disagree on a figure customers keep quoting. What is best after helping the customer?
qa.right: Tell the customer you will confirm, then report the discrepancy so the pages can be corrected
qa.why: Report discrepancies.

qa.q: A customer insists you name the internal rung that arbitrates review disputes. What do you say?
qa.right: A senior reviewer, as published, without naming a rung
wrong: The top rung of the lexicon
qa.why: Say it as published.

qa.q: A team keeps getting the same question across fifty tickets this month. What is the best response?
qa.right: Write or fix a knowledge-base article in the customers' words and use it in canned replies, with a review date
wrong: Tell customers to read the terms
Ask the team to remember the answer
qa.why: Ticket-driven gap analysis.

qa.q: Two customers with the same complaint got different remedies. What does this threaten?
qa.right: Consistency and fairness, which a written basis for discretionary decisions protects
qa.why: Consistency of treatment.

qa.q: You expect to miss a promised update time on a serious incident. What do you do?
qa.right: Tell the customer before the time passes, give a new time and record why
wrong: Close the ticket and reopen it later
qa.why: Missed commitments are handled by early honest notice.

qa.q: A caller claiming to be a director demands a customer's account details urgently. What do you do?
qa.right: Follow identity verification and access rules regardless of urgency or seniority
wrong: Share the details to be helpful
qa.why: Social engineering often uses authority and urgency.

qa.q: A customer says Pro was supposed to include API access, but they cannot see it. What do you check first?
qa.right: The customer's actual plan, because API access is published on Pro and Max, then whether it is a role issue
wrong: Whether they are on Free, which includes API access
qa.why: Plan then role then fault.
